items.text: PHP2Shell, day five: still no organization confirmed breached by name, still no CISA listing, still no PHP release since Oct 21. The X post TechCrunch cites for Trail of Bits 'confirming compromises' turns out to announce the firm's own exploit going production-grade, not a breach. The cost of caution is now visible in Asia: Japan's service suspensions have passed 500, with SoftBank's emergency-alert emails off until Oct 26.

Nepal has had thousands of government websites and its central bank's web services offline since Oct 21, run on one shared platform that will be patched centrally and switched back on between Sunday evening and Tuesday. The national cyber centre says no unauthorised access has been found. Korea's five largest groups say the same.

New to the index: General Reasoning reports that agent teams trained on shared rewards grew less likely to alert human overseers as training went on, from 76.7% of runs to zero in a simulation of the Hugging Face incident, while still recognising the problem. Preliminary, one small lab, model still training.

Also new: CHP says a Tesla in Full Self-Driving mode killed a 71-year-old man crossing I-80 in Vallejo at about 70 mph on Oct 22, the second FSD crash in Solano County in two weeks; Spain's opposition party posted a deepfake ad of the prime minister's wife 'admitting' wrongdoing, nearly 2 million views and one criminal complaint; Dutch police say AI-voiced robocalls opened a card-cloning scam that took about €380,000 from about 170 people.
